conventions.convention: Assume the Axiom of Choice; X is deterministic, has full column rank, and satisfies 1 ≤ p < n; errors are independent N(0, σ²) with σ² > 0.
The residual degrees of freedom are ν = n − p; s² = RSS_F/ν, whereas the Gaussian variance MLE is RSS_F/n. The t and F statistics are assigned zero on their zero-denominator events.
The reduced design has rank p − q, is nested in the full design, and satisfies 1 ≤ q ≤ p. The null is Xβ ∈ col(X_R); the empty reduced space is allowed when q = p.
R has positive diagonal and Q has orthonormal columns; the completion [Q Q₀] is orthogonal and P_X = QQᵀ.
Confidence levels satisfy 0 < α < 1. A zero predictor gives a singleton mean interval with coverage one. Prediction coverage includes an independent future N(0, σ²) error.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, deterministic full-column-rank X ∈ R^(n×p), 1 ≤ p < n, β ∈ R^p, σ² > 0, and independent N(0, σ²) errors. Then β̂ has law N_p(β, σ²(XᵀX)⁻¹), is independent of RSS_F, RSS_F/σ² has law χ²_(n−p), s > 0 almost surely, and every nonzero-contrast T_c has law t_(n−p). For the stated nested reduced design, under Xβ ∈ col(X_R), the partial F statistic has law F_(q,n−p). The stated tests have size exactly α. The joint MLE is (β̂, RSS_F/n) almost surely; no maximizer exists when RSS_F = 0.
Let n > p ≥ 1 and let X ∈ R^(n×p) have full column rank. Then X = QR with QᵀQ = I_p and R upper triangular with positive diagonal. Q admits an orthonormal completion [Q Q₀], and X(XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀ = QQᵀ.

In the stated full-rank Gaussian regression model, with 0 < α < 1 and t* = t_(ν,1−α/2), the interval cᵀβ̂ ± t*s√(cᵀ(XᵀX)⁻¹c) has exact coverage 1−α for cᵀβ when c ≠ 0. The mean-response interval has exact coverage 1−α when x₀ ≠ 0 and coverage one when x₀ = 0. For an independent future Gaussian response, the prediction interval x₀ᵀβ̂ ± t*s√(1+h₀) has coverage 1−α.

concerns.concern: Fact F5 says: “Student t_k is a ratio of an independent standard normal and χ_k²/k”. This omits the square root: the opened def-student-t-and-f-laws defines G/√(Q_k/k). The literal fact therefore states the wrong ratio law. Proof step 2.1 uses the correct square root, so this finding concerns the false supplier restatement rather than the theorem's actual pivot derivation.

seams_checked.note: The opened fixed-design definition and least-squares/estimability results match F14–F17 and steps 1.1/2.1. The first-moment model supplies no Gaussian assumption; this consumer states Gaussianity separately. Holding σ² fixed gives the supplier's β-indexed experiment. Full rank supplies the unique coefficients and all contrast representatives.
